text: Everyone in Dune chants Lisan al-Gaib... but what does it actually mean in Arabic?
The Qur'an says it came down in a clear Arabic lisan: a clear Arabic tongue.
Your turn. On the first page of al-Baqarah, the believers believe in this:
The UNSEEN! Everything hidden from our eyes. And it's ghayb, with a 'gh'.
So Lisan al-Ghayb means: the tongue of the unseen. The one who speaks what no one else can see.
And Frank Herbert didn't invent it. Over five hundred years before Dune, the Persian poet Hafez was already called Lisan al-Ghayb.
